content: These references are formatted in a bibliographic style, listing authors, titles, journal names, publication years, volumes, and page numbers. 1. Ng V et al. conducted a study on the spatial distribution of household tuberculosis transmission in southern China, focusing on the influence of socioeconomic status and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypes. This research was published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2019. 2. Dahiwale N, Rao S, Singh J, and colleagues emphasized the importance of family surveys of index cases for detecting tuberculosis. Their findings were published in Indian Pediatrics in 2011. 3. Duarte R, Neto M, Carvalho A, and others explored methods to improve tuberculosis contact tracing, particularly through evaluations conducted in home and workplace settings. This study appeared in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2012. 4. Ferreira TF, Matsuoka PdA, Santos AM, et al. compared the tuberculin skin test with interferon-gamma release assays for diagnosing latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Their work was published in the Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical in 2015. 5. Hanjiu W, Lili W, Guoli L, and colleagues developed a TB assay to identify tuberculosis infection in children. This research was published in Acta Medica Mediterranea in 2013. 6. Hu Y, Zhao Q, Graviss EA, et al. evaluated a TB assay for screening latent tuberculosis infection among TB contacts in Shanghai, China. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infection in 2012. 7. Huerga H, Sanchez-Padilla E, Melikyan N, and others conducted a prospective cohort study on child contacts of patients with drug-resistant tuberculosis, reporting a high prevalence of infection but a low incidence of disease. This study was published in Archives of Disease in Childhood in 2019. 8. Jia Z, Cheng S, Ma Y, et al. investigated the tuberculosis burden in China, highlighting the high prevalence of pulmonary tuberculosis among household contacts, both symptomatic and asymptomatic. Their research was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014. 9. Jones-Lopez EC, Kim S, Fregona G, et al. examined the role of cough and Mycobacterium tuberculosis strain type as risk factors for increased transmission within households. This study was published in PLOS One in 2014. 10. Josaphat J, Dias JG, Salvador S, et al. explored which tuberculosis patients fail to identify their contacts. Their findings were published in the Revista Portuguesa de Pneumologia in 2014. 11. Kuan MM, Yang HL, Wu HS studied tuberculosis among newly arrived foreign spouses in Taiwan before obtaining citizenship, covering the years 2006–2011. This research was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014. 12. Kwon Y, Kim SJ, Kim J, et al. reported on the outcomes of tuberculosis contact investigations in congregate settings in Korea in 2013. Their findings were published in Osong Public Health and Research Perspectives in 2014. 13. Leung EC, Leung CC, Kam KM, et al. investigated the transmission of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis in a metropolitan city. This study was published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2013. 14. Leung CC, Yam WC, Ho PL, et al. demonstrated that TB assays outperform the tuberculin skin test in predicting the development of active tuberculosis among household contacts. Their research was published in Respirology in 2015. 15. Lin CZ, Wang FF, Li JF, et al. analyzed the chemoprophylactic effects on close contacts of patients with active tuberculosis and positive tuberculin skin tests. This study was published in Family Medicine and Community Health in 2014. 16. Loredo C, Cailleaux-Cezar M, Efron A, et al. compared two programmatic approaches for close contact tracing from tuberculosis index cases in a retrospective quasi-experimental study. Their findings were published in BMC Pulmonary Medicine in 2014. 17. Mendes MA, Gaio R, Reis R, et al. investigated whether contact screening in tuberculosis can identify individuals at higher risk. This study was published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2013. 18. Rajan JV, Ferrazoli L, Waldman EA, et al. found that diabetes increases the risk of recent-transmission tuberculosis among household contacts in São Paulo, Brazil. Their research was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2017. 19. Ribeiro-Rodrigues R, Kim S, Coelho da Silva FD, et al. reported on the discordance between tuberculin skin tests and interferon-gamma release assays in recently exposed household contacts of pulmonary TB cases in Brazil. This study was published in PLOS One in 2014. 20. Verhagen LM, Maes M, Villalba JA, et al. assessed the agreement between the QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube test and the tuberculin skin test, as well as predictors of positive test results in Warao Amerindian pediatric tuberculosis contacts. Their findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014.
